title: The people around the king
summary: Character roles from the agreed design. **No final character art or dialogue exists yet.** Established actions and possible accusations are deliberately separated. “Review” means design recorded, not an implemented asset.

items.title: The king
items.body:
**Accepted role:** victim in the ceremony; skeletal-headed host in the gallery.

His only question: *How did I die, and who killed me?*

**Mind access:** blocked. He is the only unreadable character.

**Production needs:** stand, take a grape, walk, eat, show distress and collapse; seated gallery pose. Final appearance is not designed.

items.title: The queen
items.body:
**Established suspicion:** she has considered poisoning the king; his meals have been sent with her approval.

Intent must not be treated as proof of the fatal act. Thoughts must reflect what she actually knows.

**Open:** visual design, exact thoughts and event timing.

items.title: The aide
items.body:
**Observed action:** fills the king’s cup.

**Possible player theory:** poison in the drink, perhaps arranged with the count. Neither poisoning nor the conspiracy is established as fact.

**Open:** name, motive, thought text and animation.

items.title: The count
items.body:
**Answer candidate:** the count conspired with the aide to poison the king.

This is a possible deduction, not a confirmed plot event. Do not write omniscient thoughts that turn a hypothesis into fact.

**Open:** identity, behavior and whether any conspiracy was actually attempted.

items.title: The guards
items.body:
**Accepted action:** intervene, surround the king and walk him away. They do not pick him up or carry him.

**Player theory:** a guard stabbed him from behind in the chaos. This is not established fact.

**Open:** guard count, exact routes, thought groups and coordinated animations.

items.title: The attackers
items.body:
**Accepted action:** several people rush forward from the crowd. A crossbow is heard and a knife is thrown toward the king.

The attack is real but does not cause his death.

**Open:** identities, projectile paths, exact choreography and thoughts.

items.title: The wedding party & court
items.body:
**Accepted setting:** the prince is marrying; the royal family, bride’s family and state officials sit at the raised table. Other guests stand beyond an open buffer.

**Open:** crowd size, distinct readable characters, reactions and names. Keep the jam scope compact.
